life_history: Jill is an adult woman who recently got divorced and moved to Portland. She has been struggling with high blood pressure that has been difficult to lower. To cope with the transition and socialize, she began visiting a local pub about four times a week, drinking 3 to 6 glasses of wine per occasion. Her son has expressed concern about her drinking, and she recently fell on her way home from the bar, injuring her shoulder. She presented for a routine medical visit regarding her blood pressure, where an annual screening revealed her drinking is in the harmful category.
core_belief_description: I am bound to be alone
intermediate_beliefs: Positive assumption: If I go to the pub and drink wine, then I can socialize and cope with my loneliness; negative assumption: If I stop drinking and going to the pub, then the isolation and distress of my divorce will overwhelm me.
intermediate_beliefs_during_depression: If I try to cut back on my drinking and fail, it proves that I lack willpower and am destined to remain lonely and unhealthy.
coping_strategies: Maladaptive coping includes drinking 3-6 glasses of wine multiple times a week to socialize and manage the stress of a divorce and moving, as well as initially downplaying the risks of her drinking. Adaptive secondary harm-reduction attempts discussed include tracking drink counts, aiming for less than three drinks per night and under seven per week, and reducing pub visits to a couple of times a week without fully quitting.

cognitive_models.situation: Experiencing isolation and adjusting to life after getting divorced and moving to Portland.
cognitive_models.automatic_thoughts: I need to socialize. Going down to the little pub and having a few glasses of wine will help.
cognitive_models.behavior: Going to the pub four times a week and drinking three to six glasses of wine.

cognitive_models.situation: The counselor points out that her drinking score places her in the harmful category and exceeds that of 90 percent of clinic patients.
cognitive_models.automatic_thoughts: Seven drinks in a week doesn't seem like that much. My drinking has increased a little since I got divorced, but I don't think it's that much of a problem.
cognitive_models.behavior: Downplaying the severity of her alcohol consumption and minimizing the problem.

cognitive_models.situation: The counselor explains that drinking may be pushing her blood pressure up, reminding her of a recent fall and her son's concerns.
cognitive_models.automatic_thoughts: I didn't realize drinking was related to blood pressure. It's scary to think my drinking is harmful. I don't think I need to quit, but I can try to cut down.
cognitive_models.behavior: Agreeing to a harm-reduction plan to drink no more than seven glasses a week and reduce pub visits.
